title: 2015 AMC 8 Problem 25
statement: One-inch squares are cut from the corners of this \(5\) inch square. What is the area in square inches of the largest square that can be fitted into the remaining space?

solutions.text:
For a largest fitted square, each side must touch an inner corner of one of the removed \(1\)-inch squares; otherwise the fitted square could be enlarged. Thus it surrounds the central \(3\times3\) square and adds four congruent right triangles, one along each side.

The central square has area \(3\cdot3=9.\) Each added triangle has base \(3\) and height \(1,\) so the four triangles have total area \[4\left(\dfrac{3\cdot1}{2}\right)=6.\]

The fitted square has area \(9+6=15.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: The fitted square can be tilted around the central \(3\times3\) square.
Add the central square area and the four congruent corner triangles.
